texts: mixed: the arriving, the hall and the every-morning recurrence are all recorded, but they stack onto each individual thread, so the parse ends up saying every thread arrives every morning rather than that threads arrive each morning. Rewrite as "The threads arrive at Cauldron Hall each morning." -- the definite plural makes it one arrival of the threads that recurs daily, which is the reading you mean.
good. the per-Keeper rule covers the leaving, the night's threads, the wicker basket and its place at the Hall door, with nothing extra invented.
good. the weighing, the threads and the "by mid-morning" deadline are all covered.
good. the portioning, the threads and the three cauldrons as destination are all covered, with the count on the cauldrons kept.
good. the drawing, the sea-water and the cisterns as source are all covered.

bad: the "submerged" state is recorded of the bundle of threads as one object rather than of each thread, so no individual thread comes out submerged; the clausal "until" also has no proper endpoint form, so the stopping condition is recorded loosely whatever you do. Rewrite as "Hesper pours sea-water over the threads until every thread is submerged." -- the explicit "every" forces the state down onto the individual threads.
good. the banked central hearth, the lighting and the cauldron fires are all covered.
good. "never goes out" comes out as a flat denial that the hearth ever goes out, with the phrasal verb kept whole rather than split.
